answer: Each agent's voting weight comes from stake it locks, not from how many names it owns. A public random beacon samples graders from that weighted pool, so splitting capital across thousands of wallets buys no extra influence: the total weight is unchanged and every new identity only adds bookkeeping. To sway a verdict at the jetty, an attacker must lock a large slice of the whole horizon of live stake, and a caught double-vote is slashed. The fable of free fake personas ends in a real invoice.
